title: Balwaan
character_social_background: Poor family; lives in a small, shabby tenement with his mother and sister
role_gist: Arjun Singh, a poor college student, falls for Deepa, the Police Commissioner's daughter, and is jailed for attacking a corrupt officer. Deepa bails him out, and her father, who wants honest men in the force, makes him a policeman. Posted to a city where his predecessor was murdered, he takes on the gangster Bhaiji, who has the community shun his family until his mother and sister die, and then frames him for murder.
principal_motivation: To clean up the city Bhaiji controls, and then to avenge his family.
principal_conflict: A gangster who turns a whole community against an honest officer and his family.
character_arc: From an angry student jailed for hitting a corrupt policeman to the honest officer the commissioner wanted; the summary breaks off with him framed and arrested.
character_outcome: Not documented; the Wikipedia summary ends with Arjun escaping Bhaiji's chains only to be arrested for a murder he was framed for.
recognition: Shetty's debut as a leading man. Filmfare's retrospective on Divya Bharti calls her the established star of the film and a big factor in its success.
research_notes: Box Office India's archived 1992 table lists Balwaan 25th of 25 with no figures or verdict (SOURCE-135); the verdict 'Hit' comes from a Filmfare retrospective on Divya Bharti (SOURCE-152), not from a trade figure. The Wikipedia plot ends with Arjun framed and arrested, so his outcome and the romance's are undocumented (PAIR-001). Film Information (SOURCE-159) names Balwaan as the first of seven Shetty films 'released from his office'.

principal_motivation: To win Mamta and protect his new friends.
principal_conflict: Colonel Chikara's terrorists, who want back the nuclear material accidentally left in Vikas's car.
character_arc: From a brawler kept in check by a borrowed nerd's disguise to a hero whose strength is put to use.

role_gist: Yeda Anna Shetty, brother of the Welcome don Uday Shetty, and Romeo, Majnu's brother, are gangsters owed money by the directors Dev and Das. They force the directors to cast them prominently in a ₹2,000 crore film designed to flop. Yeda Anna develops a rivalry with the washed-up star Rajiv, and when the shoot moves to a village under real terrorist threat, the crew's fake rescue mission becomes a real fight for survival.

critical_reception: Mixed. Film Information: 'Sunil Shetty is very good as Yeda Anna.' Bollywood Hungama (3.5/5): 'Suniel Shetty and Arshad Warsi brilliantly add to the madness.' Hindustan Times (3 stars) credits Akshay Kumar's 'effortless chemistry with his Hera Pheri team', Shetty included. The Indian Express (1.5 stars) found it 'rarely madcap enough'; India Today notes only that 'a rivalry is established between Rajeev and Yeda Anna'.
recognition: Third film of the Welcome series; reunites him with his Hera Pheri co-stars Akshay Kumar and Paresh Rawal.
